metadata.title: ACCP v2.0 Native Route Bus, TUI Mode Picker, Compiler Package, Runtime Gate, and Multi-Agent Artifact Communication
metadata.description: P49 implements ACCP v2.0 as a native YAML-to-compiled-JSON communication and routing substrate for Pi. The phase introduces the standalone packages/accp-compiler package, the 24-report registry, strict schemas for gate-critical report types, compiled route signals, gate verdicts, artifact emission, Tab-driven ACCP mode selection in TUI, InitialRouteIndicator and AccpTaskEnvelope, runtime authority checks, completion gate integration, event/read-model/dashboard visibility, repair/canonicalization loop, and multi-agent ACCP route bus. PlanSpec v5 remains the authority boundary for allowed files, commands, validation, mutation, and completion constraints. ACCP route signals recommend next tasks but never authorize execution by themselves. The repository-root `accp_v2_0_package/` directory is treated as the local source package for ACCP v2.0 documentation, examples, prompt contracts, schemas, and registry metadata and must be heavily referenced throughout the implementation.

intent.summary: P49 is the phase where ACCP stops being only a report convention and becomes a first-class runtime-visible artifact flow. The implementation must not blur authority boundaries. User-selected initial modes, agent-recommended next routes, compiler-normalized route signals, and runtime-authorized execution are four distinct stages.

routing.nextRouteOwner: compiled ACCP route-signal.json from prior report

operatorNotes: The accp_v2_0_package directory is read-only in P49.
Rendered Markdown is a preview and must not be parsed for execution.
Compiler diagnostics are machine-readable and must be surfaced in TUI/dashboard.
Repair loops may correct structure but must not invent evidence or alter command results.

commandClasses.title: Local ACCP YAML compile and validation commands

mission.text: Implement ACCP v2.0 native compiler, route bus, TUI mode picker, runtime gate integration, and multi-agent compiled artifact communication while preserving PlanSpec as the execution authority.

hardRequirements.text: PlanSpec v5 does not choose the next ACCP mode. PlanSpec defines authority, required reports, allowed files, command policy, and completion constraints. Next task routing is driven by compiled ACCP RouteSignal emitted from the previous report, and runtime applies PlanSpec authority checks before allowing any route to execute.

The repository-root accp_v2_0_package directory must be used as the local source bundle for ACCP v2.0 documentation, examples, prompts, registry metadata, and schema sketches. It must be referenced heavily and remain read-only during P49.
Tab in the TUI opens the ACCP mode picker, not the file picker. File/path selection moves to @ mention and/or Ctrl+P. The selected initial mode produces an InitialRouteIndicator and AccpTaskEnvelope.

The ACCP compiler must be deterministic TypeScript. LLMs may assist with bounded repair/canonicalization, but compiler verdicts, evidence validation, route normalization, and runtime authority must not depend on LLM judgment.

Runtime consumers must read compiled ACCP JSON artifacts, route-signal.json, gate-verdict.json, index.json, and graph.json. Runtime must not parse raw ACCP YAML or rendered Markdown for authority decisions.

antiPatterns.text: Do not create packages/accp-compiler and then keep coding-agent using a separate shadow parser.
Do not treat next_route as permission to mutate. RouteSignal is advisory until runtime checks PlanSpec authority.
Do not hide machine-critical behavior in prose. Report types, gate verdicts, route decisions, diagnostics, and evidence must be structured.
Do not paste the full ACCP specification into every worker prompt. Use compact prompt contracts loaded from templates and registry.
Do not parse generated Markdown preview for execution. Rendered Markdown is human-facing only.

operatorNotes.text: Initial route is user/TUI driven; subsequent route is compiled-artifact driven.
ACCP required mode should not become default until all W1-W8 gates pass.
The accp_v2_0_package root directory is intentionally referenced as a source package, but runtime code must depend on compiled local TypeScript modules rather than reading package prose at runtime.

waves.title: Authority, Package Intake, and Contract Foundation
waves.description: Establish the local ACCP v2.0 package as read-only design input, update PlanSpec authority semantics for ACCP v2.0, and create additive execution-contract types. This wave must not alter runtime behavior. Its primary purpose is to create stable shared vocabulary for the rest of P49: report types, support levels, modes, route signals, gate verdicts, diagnostics, task envelopes, and optional worker ACCP output.

waves.title: Standalone Compiler Core
waves.description: Create `packages/accp-compiler` and implement the deterministic source, schema, registry, ID, reference, lineage, and evidence validation foundations. This wave is intentionally compiler-heavy because P49 must not rely on LLM judgment for runtime truth. The existing PlanSpec compiler architecture should be used as conceptual precedent, but the new compiler package must be independent and reusable.

waves.title: Compiler Outputs, Route Signals, Gate Verdicts, Artifacts, and CLI
waves.description: Complete the ACCP compiler output chain: route-signal.json, gate-verdict.json, compiled.json, ir.json, index.json, graph.json, rendered Markdown, and CLI commands. This wave turns the compiler from a validator into a producer of runtime-readable artifacts, while still keeping runtime authority outside the compiler.

waves.title: Prompt Integration and Worker Compile Hook
waves.description: Make coding-agent ACCP-aware without making every prompt enormous. This wave introduces compact prompt contracts, AgentSession/system prompt injection, workspace prompt injection, and autonomous executor compile hooks. It is the first wave that touches live worker execution flow, so all behavior must be gated by ACCP mode.

waves.title: Runtime Gate, Events, Read Model, and API Visibility
waves.description: Wire ACCP artifacts into authoritative runtime control and visibility. CompletionGateV2 and TransitionRouter become ACCP verdict-aware in required mode; event journal records ACCP compile/gate/finding/route lifecycle; execution-service and web-server expose read-only views. This wave is high-risk because it touches completion and transition paths.

waves.title: TUI Mode Selection and Initial Route Envelope
waves.description: Make the human-facing terminal workflow ACCP-native. Tab becomes the ACCP mode picker. File selection moves to @ mention and/or Ctrl+P. InitialRouteIndicator and AccpTaskEnvelope bridge free-form user intent into structured initial task routing, while subsequent mode progression remains driven by compiled route signals.

waves.title: ACCP Route Bus, Repair Loop, Dashboard, and Artifact Store
waves.description: Introduce P49's multi-agent coordination layer. The ACCP Route Bus moves compiled artifacts between scout, fixer, validator, reviewer, and coordinator agents. Repair loop makes compiler failures recoverable without granting LLMs authority. Dashboard and artifact store expose the route graph and compiled evidence to humans.

waves.title: Template Expansion, End-to-End Gauntlets, Final Promotion, and P50 Readiness
waves.description: Finish P49 by expanding non-critical report family templates, running end-to-end gauntlets, producing operator documentation, and creating final promotion evidence. This wave should prove the complete route sequence from mode picker to compiled report to route signal to runtime authority check to dashboard visibility.

workspaces.title: ACCP v2.0 Package Intake, Root Reference, and Local Source Contract
workspaces.description:
ACCP v2.0 Package Intake, Root Reference, and Local Source Contract


Establish the local repository-root `accp_v2_0_package/` directory as the read-only source package for ACCP v2.0 during P49. This workspace must create a typed reference contract that records where the package lives, which subdirectories are authoritative for docs, examples, prompt contracts, registry metadata, and schema sketches, and how implementation code may cite those assets without copying unstable prose into runtime logic. The worker must not mutate the package. The worker must add a small metadata module in execution-contracts that exposes constants such as `ACCP_V2_PACKAGE_ROOT`, `ACCP_V2_PACKAGE_DOCS`, `ACCP_V2_PACKAGE_SCHEMAS`, `ACCP_V2_PACKAGE_PROMPTS`, `ACCP_V2_PACKAGE_REGISTRY`, and `ACCP_V2_PACKAGE_EXAMPLES`, plus documentation explaining that this package is a design-time and fixture source, not a runtime authority store.


This workspace must be implemented as a production-wired change, not as a loose artifact, not as a documentation-only placeholder, and not as an isolated module that nobody imports. The worker must preserve the existing Pi authority model: PlanSpec defines allowed files, command policies, write boundaries, report requirements, lock requirements, and hard stops; ACCP v2.0 provides compiled evidence, route signals, gate verdicts, and structured communication artifacts. The worker must not give ACCP reports authority to mutate repository state, transition workspace state, bypass write gates, bypass command policy, or promote plans. Any route suggestion produced from ACCP must be treated as advisory until the runtime authority layer verifies it against PlanSpec, workspace state, command policy, write gate, and human-confirmation requirements.

The implementation must heavily reference the repository-root `accp_v2_0_package/` directory. That package is the canonical local source bundle for ACCP v2.0 in this phase and contains docs, examples, prompts, registry metadata, and schema sketches. The worker must treat the package as read-only input and must not edit it unless a later PlanSpec explicitly grants ownership. Any template, schema, diagnostic code, support matrix, or example fixture copied or adapted from that package must preserve attribution in comments or metadata where the local codebase convention allows it.

The implementation must preserve backward compatibility with existing free-text worker reports while introducing ACCP-native structured outputs. Where an existing field such as `report: string` is mandatory, the new ACCP structure must be optional and additive. Existing non-ACCP workflows must continue to run with ACCP mode set to `off`. P49 may introduce route bus capabilities, but it must not force every worker to become ACCP-native immediately.

Validation must include positive and negative tests. Negative tests are mandatory because this phase is fundamentally about trust boundaries: invalid YAML, missing required sections, unresolved route targets, mutation without authority, pass verdict without command evidence, and promotion with blockers must all be tested explicitly. Tests must demonstrate that the compiler, TUI, route bus, runtime gate, event journal, and read model fail closed where appropriate.
